entities.name: PMID:25429008
observations: Jin et al. (2015) studied field pea in phosphorus-deficient Vertisol using soil columns in a SoilFACE CO2-enrichment system.
Treatments were 15 or 60 mg P kg−1 soil and ambient 380–400 or elevated 550–580 ppm CO2; drought began at flowering.

entities.name: Pisum sativum
observations: In the directly relevant study, adequate phosphorus increased soluble sugars, leaf inorganic phosphate, and deeper root-length distribution during drought.

Elevated CO2 reduced stomatal conductance and transpiration, increased soluble sugars and relative leaf water content, and improved water-use efficiency; the greatest water-use efficiency occurred with adequate phosphorus plus elevated CO2.

entities.name: Phosphorus-deficient Vertisol
observations: The experimental soil was phosphorus-deficient Vertisol, with deficient and adequate phosphorus treatments.

entities.name: P-CO2 drought tolerance
observations: The authors concluded that phosphorus application and elevated CO2 interactively enhanced periodic drought tolerance in field pea.
Direct evidence supports improved water relations and physiological acclimation; the accessible abstract does not quantify biomass, yield, or photosynthetic-rate enhancement.
